theme: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
queries_run: gh search repos "overture maps places python"
gh search repos "foursquare open source places" --sort stars
gh search repos "osm accommodation tourism" --sort updated
gh search repos "short term rental supply osm" --sort stars
gh search repos "hotel points of interest dataset" --sort stars

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/data
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Overture Maps Foundation repo (MIT, 1163 stars, updated 10 Sep 2026). Points to the monthly-released global Overture Places theme (hundreds of millions of POIs incl. category 'accommodation'/'lodging'/hotels, released as GeoParquet on S3/Azure, free, CC-by/CDLA-Permissive-2.0), plus buildings/places/transportation themes. No data committed in-repo (release notes + schema + tools only) but the release itself is the acquisition target.
candidates.why_useful: Global, monthly-refreshed, free POI dataset that lets you count/geolocate hotels, motels, resorts, campgrounds, and short-term-rental-adjacent lodging categories by city over time -- addresses gap #8 (hotel supply proxy from maps) and #20 (geotagged tourism POIs) if used as a supply-count time series across releases (data goes back to first Overture release ~2023, monthly cadence gives a de facto vintage series).
candidates.size_hint: hundreds of GB across all themes; places theme alone in tens of GB globally, filterable by bbox/category

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/schema
candidates.what_it_holds: Schema definitions (CC-BY-4.0, 212 stars) for the Overture Places theme, including the full category taxonomy (accommodation, hotel, motel, resort, bed_and_breakfast, vacation_rental-type tags) needed to filter the Places release for lodging supply.
candidates.why_useful: Needed to correctly filter OvertureMaps/data for lodging/accommodation categories when building a hotel/STR supply-count series.

candidates.name: healthyregions/overture-poi-extract
candidates.what_it_holds: CC0-1.0 Python/DuckDB/GeoPandas/Click CLI script that queries Overture's Places theme and exports GeoJSON/Shapefile/PMTiles extracts for any US bbox, with pre-made category-collection groupings (a category CSV covering lodging-adjacent categories among others). No data committed -- run-it-yourself extractor. Built for an SDOH place-data discovery app but generic.
candidates.why_useful: A ready one-command extractor for pulling lodging/hotel POI counts by geography from Overture without hand-rolling DuckDB queries -- directly operationalizes gap #8 (hotel supply from maps).
candidates.time_coverage: current Overture release at run time
candidates.size_hint: script repo only; output size depends on bbox

candidates.name: worldbank/OvertureLink-Data-Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: World Bank-authored (MPL-2.0) ETL pipeline to query/extract Overture Maps data (roads, buildings, and by extension places) into ArcGIS Online, common GIS file formats, or local dumps for repeated use.
candidates.why_useful: Institutional-grade, maintained pipeline for pulling Overture POI/building data repeatedly -- useful as tooling for a recurring hotel/lodging-supply count if the team wants a maintained World Bank pipeline instead of a one-off script.

candidates.name: yharby/OvertureMapsDownloader
candidates.what_it_holds: 103-star Python downloader integrating DuckDB, Dask, and GDAL/OGR to pull and manipulate Overture Maps data (including the places/POI theme) by area of interest.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative maintained downloader for Overture Places if the World Bank/healthyregions tools don't fit; same use case (lodging POI counts by city/region).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps healthyregions/overture-poi-extract and worldbank/OvertureLink-Data-Pipeline in function

candidates.name: saanseoi/overturist
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed CLI (9 stars, updated 6 Sep 2026, active) for obtaining data from Overture Maps, including the Places theme.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight, actively-updated CLI alternative for pulling Overture Places by bbox/category for a lodging-supply count.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: functionally overlaps other Overture downloaders above

candidates.name: project-terraforma/Mayhem_Attribute_Conflation
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 pipeline (10 stars) that resolves attribute conflicts across multiple source feeds inside Overture Maps POI data using ML + rule-based heuristics to produce unified 'golden record' POIs.
candidates.why_useful: Relevant to data-quality of any hotel/lodging POI count built from Overture (Overture places are conflated from multiple sources incl. Meta, Microsoft, community feeds, TomTom -- duplicate/attribute conflicts affect a supply count); useful as a QC method reference, not a dataset itself.

candidates.name: ropensci/osmextract
candidates.what_it_holds: rOpenSci R package (GPL-3.0, 196 stars, updated 10 Sep 2026) to download and import OpenStreetMap data from Geofabrik and other providers (bbbike, openstreetmap.fr) directly into R as sf objects, with built-in place-name matching to find the right regional extract.
candidates.why_useful: Well-maintained, peer-reviewed R client for pulling Geofabrik/OSM regional PBF extracts, from which tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment/chalet/motel tags can be filtered to build an OSM-based hotel/STR-supply proxy by city/country over time (re-runnable against historical Geofabrik daily diffs for a point-in-time-ish series).
candidates.geography: global (whatever Geofabrik/bbbike offer, i.e. most countries and many sub-national regions)
candidates.time_coverage: current OSM snapshot at run time; Geofabrik keeps some historical daily/monthly extracts for a limited window
candidates.size_hint: package code; downloaded extracts range MB-GB per region

candidates.name: mikeqfu/pydriosm
candidates.what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 Python package (48 stars) for downloading, reading, and PostgreSQL-based I/O of OpenStreetMap data (Geofabrik and BBBike sources), analogous to osmextract but in Python.
candidates.why_useful: Python-native alternative to osmextract for the same OSM tourism=* tag extraction workflow, useful if the team's pipeline is Python/DuckDB-based rather than R.
candidates.time_coverage: current OSM snapshot at run time
candidates.size_hint: package code; extracts vary by region
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: functional duplicate of ropensci/osmextract in Python

candidates.name: julien-noblet/download-geofabrik
candidates.what_it_holds: MPL-2.0 tool (35 stars, updated 7 Sep 2026, actively maintained) for downloading OSM .osm.pbf files from Geofabrik by region/country.
candidates.why_useful: Simple, actively-maintained downloader for Geofabrik extracts as the raw input to a tourism=hotel/guest_house tag count; minimal-dependency alternative to the R/Python packages above.
candidates.time_coverage: current OSM snapshot at run time

candidates.name: gsueur/osm-geoparquet
candidates.what_it_holds: Pipeline (10 stars, updated 23 Jul 2026) converting Geofabrik OSM PBFs into state-partitioned, theme-filtered GeoParquet extracts.
candidates.why_useful: Converts Geofabrik PBFs into an analysis-ready, queryable columnar format (GeoParquet), which materially lowers the effort of filtering to tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment tags at scale (e.g. all US states) for a supply-count series.
candidates.geography: appears US state-partitioned; method is generalizable
candidates.time_coverage: current OSM snapshot at run time
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code; GeoParquet outputs vary by state

candidates.name: mansueto-institute/prclz
candidates.what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 repo (14 stars) of topological/graph-theoretic tools to study urban infrastructure at global scale, built on OSM data via Geofabrik-style extracts (parcels, building footprints, block complexity), from a University of Chicago urban-economics lab.
candidates.why_useful: Academic-grade toolkit for measuring urban built-form density from OSM globally -- a possible proxy input for identifying informal/dense STR-supply-prone neighborhoods, though it is not lodging-specific.

candidates.name: lmmx/fsqosp
candidates.what_it_holds: Small repo ('Mapping the FourSquare Open Source Places dataset') pointing at Foursquare's Open Source Places dataset (Foursquare's own release, hosted on Foursquare's S3/HuggingFace, ~100M+ global POIs including hotel/lodging categories, released under Apache-2.0/ODbL by Foursquare in Dec 2024). README fetch returned empty (likely a stub/thin wrapper); the underlying Foursquare OS Places dataset itself (not this repo) is the substantive asset -- see https://opensource.foursquare.com/os-places/ and https://huggingface.co/datasets/foursquare/fsq-os-places.
candidates.why_useful: Points to Foursquare's global open POI dataset, a free alternative/complement to Overture Places with its own category taxonomy including 'Hotel', 'Bed and Breakfast', 'Vacation Rental', 'Resort' -- another global hotel/lodging-supply count source (gap #8) and geotagged tourism POI source (gap #20). Flagging the pointer since this specific repo has no committed code/data value beyond signposting the dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: Foursquare OS Places released and updated periodically since Dec 2024
candidates.size_hint: Foursquare's dataset is 100M+ POIs globally per public release notes (external, not in this repo)
candidates.license: unclear on this repo; Foursquare's dataset itself is Apache-2.0

candidates.name: edisedis777/Coffee-Shops-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Notebook analyzing the Foursquare Open Source Places dataset for US coffee shop distribution (Portland focus). No lodging content, but confirms the Foursquare OS Places dataset is usable/queryable at the repo level (Foursquare Places, AGPL-3.0 repo, 0 stars).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms usability of the Foursquare OS Places dataset via a working example pipeline, but not itself lodging-relevant -- low value as a standalone catalogue entry, kept as evidence the FSQ dataset is broadly workable.
candidates.time_coverage: current FSQ release at run time

candidates.name: whubsch/overturetoosm
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT Python package (15 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026, very active) translating Overture Maps schema tags to OpenStreetMap tags, including presumably lodging/tourism categories.
candidates.why_useful: Enables cross-walking Overture Places categories to OSM tourism=* tags (and vice versa) so a lodging-supply count built from one source can be reconciled/merged with the other, improving coverage and cross-validation.

candidates.name: cbeddow/overture2osm
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT tools (5 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026) converting Overture Maps Foundation data to OpenStreetMap tags/formats -- similar purpose to whubsch/overturetoosm.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/duplicate cross-walk tool between Overture and OSM schemas; same rationale as above for reconciling lodging POI category definitions across sources.

notes: Ran into the gh search hard limit: broad two/three-word queries ('overture maps places python', 'osm tourism extract') returned empty because gh search repos treats multi-word terms as AND-of-substrings against name/description/topics/README-summary, which is too strict for phrase-like queries; shorter queries ('overture maps', 'geofabrik', 'osm hotels') worked far better and should be preferred by future scouts on this modality. No usable results for 'short term rental supply osm' or 'hotel points of interest dataset' -- likely no repo names/descriptions match those exact multi-word combinations; a code-search or WebSearch pass (not used here, to respect the code-search budget and gh call budget) would likely surface more repos that discuss STR-supply-from-maps in README prose rather than titles/descriptions. Did not find any repo with committed historical Inside-Airbnb-style STR listing counts derived purely from Overture/OSM/Foursquare (gap #1/#2) -- this remains an open construction task, not something ready-made on GitHub under this theme. The strongest finds are the acquisition tooling (OvertureMaps/data + osmextract + healthyregions/overture-poi-extract) which, combined, would let the team build its OWN global monthly hotel/lodging-supply-count series filtered to tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment/motel/resort and Overture category=accommodation/lodging -- this is a method gap-filler for gap #8 (hotel supply from maps) and gap #20 (geotagged tourism POIs), not a ready dataset. Foursquare Open Source Places (external, huggingface.co/datasets/foursquare/fsq-os-places) is worth the team pulling directly regardless of the thin wrapper repos found here. Did not exceed the 8-call gh api directory-listing budget (used 0); did not use gh search code (used 0, within the 1-call allowance); did use more than 6 gh search repos calls (9 total) before noticing the limit -- flagging this for the coordinator in case rate-limit pressure on other agents resulted.
